headline: GOLD CRASHES TO $4,548 AS SCORCHING CPI DATA KILLS RATE-CUT HOPES; SILVER PLUNGES 10%
snippet: Gold fell 1.83% to $4,548/oz on May 15 and silver plunged 10.61% to $77.52/oz after April CPI came in at a hotter-than-expected 3.8% year-over-year — crushing market hopes for Federal Reserve rate cuts and triggering a synchronized selloff across equities, bonds, and commodities. Producer prices posted their steepest single-month spike since early 2022. Most institutional forecasters are holding year-end gold targets above $5,000, framing the dip as a buying opportunity with structural tailwinds intact.

headline: EQUINOX GOLD GRABS ORLA MINING IN $5.1B DEAL AS M&A WAVE SWEEPS GOLD SECTOR
snippet: Equinox Gold agreed to acquire TSX-listed Orla Mining in a $5.1 billion cash-and-stock transaction, one of two major gold M&A deals highlighted by Bloomberg on May 13 as the consolidation wave accelerates. Q1 2026 recorded 121 mining transactions worth a combined $21.6 billion — up sharply from $16.1 billion in Q1 2025 — as producers race to secure assets while gold trades near record highs. Record producer margins are fuelling a cash war chest that is now flowing into acquisitions rather than back to shareholders.

headline: FORECASTERS UNMOVED BY DIP: INSTITUTIONAL CROWD STILL SEES GOLD ABOVE $5,000 BY YEAR-END
snippet: Despite Thursday's inflation-driven selloff to $4,548/oz, major institutional forecasters are maintaining year-end gold targets well above $5,000, citing structural safe-haven demand, accelerating central bank buying, and ongoing de-dollarization. Metals Focus says 2026 highs will rise 'well above' $5,000 and that any significant dip represents a buying opportunity. The piece surveys consensus views from Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, and UBS ahead of a summer rally that many analysts still expect.

headline: ANALYST SLAPS SELL ON BARRICK DESPITE Q1 BEAT: THE $5,000 GOLD 'MIRAGE' CASE
snippet: Barrick Mining beat Q1 2026 revenue estimates by $380 million and EPS by $0.17, yet Seeking Alpha maintains a Sell, arguing that current forward EV/EBIT multiples are only attractive if gold sustains near $5,000/oz and noting that Thursday's CPI shock shows that assumption is fragile. Agnico Eagle, by contrast, posted a record quarterly operating margin with $1,483 AISC against a $4,861 realized price — cited as the better risk-adjusted long. The contrarian take is a useful counterweight against the sector euphoria narrative.

headline: GOLD MINING STOCKS POISED TO FINALLY OUTRUN THE METAL AS VALUATIONS CLOSE THE GAP
snippet: With gold up over 64% from a year ago and mining equities still trading at historic valuation discounts to the underlying metal, analysts are calling 2026 the year the gap finally closes. Senior producers with low AISC, clean balance sheets, and organic growth pipelines are set to generate record free cash flow and rising dividends. ESG-rated miners are attracting an additional institutional premium as the investor base broadens beyond traditional commodity funds.

headline: COPPER SMASHES ALL-TIME HIGH AS CHINA BANS KEY MINING CHEMICAL AND MAJOR MINES STUMBLE
snippet: Copper futures hit fresh records above $13,000/tonne on robust Chinese industrial demand as Beijing simultaneously announced a halt on sulfuric acid exports from May — a critical processing input for roughly 15% of global mine output. Grasberg in Indonesia remains underutilized after a fatal mudslide and Quebrada Blanca in Chile cut its production guidance. J.P. Morgan is projecting a 330,000-tonne refined copper shortfall in 2026, with power grid and AI infrastructure buildout absorbing every tonne of available supply.

headline: ENERGY STORAGE EXPLOSION RESCUES BEATEN-DOWN LITHIUM DEMAND OUTLOOK FOR 2026
snippet: China's power sector reforms and surging battery storage deployments have revived lithium demand faster than expected, with Morgan Stanley forecasting an 80,000-tonne LCE deficit in 2026 and UBS projecting a 22,000-tonne gap. Analysts see lithium carbonate in the 80,000–200,000 yuan/tonne range this year — a sharp recovery from the 2024-25 lows that crushed junior lithium developers. Juniors with shovel-ready projects in allied jurisdictions are getting a second look from institutional allocators.

headline: RARE EARTH PRICES TUMBLE 21% IN APRIL — CHINA QUOTA DECISION IN JUNE IS THE PIVOTAL MOMENT
snippet: NdPr oxide fell 21.0% in April to $99.61/kg — its sharpest monthly decline since the Q1 rally — pulling neodymium oxide to $108.96/kg and praseodymium to $109.60/kg. The entire complex is now holding its breath for China's mid-year MIIT mining quota announcement, expected in June, which will determine whether H2 2026 supply tightens or floods. NdPr is expected to consolidate in the $95–$115/kg domestic range through Q2 before the quota signal arrives.

headline: LUMINA METALS RAISES C$406M IN TORONTO IPO — JUNIOR MINING'S DEFINING CAPITAL RAISE OF 2026
snippet: Lumina Metals' Toronto IPO closed at C$406.2 million, the largest junior mining capital raise of 2026 and a bellwether signal that institutional capital is rotating back into the sector. The copper-uranium developer reflects the 'allied jurisdiction' trend reshaping capital allocation, as fund managers prioritize supply-chain security over raw price exposure. Multiple sector analysts called it a defining transaction in junior mining's post-2024 renaissance.

headline: AI POWER HUNGER SET TO TURBOCHARGE URANIUM DEMAND — DOE SELECTS 11 ADVANCED REACTOR PROJECTS
snippet: Artificial intelligence data centre power demand is reshaping long-term expectations for nuclear energy and uranium procurement, with the U.S. Department of Energy selecting eleven advanced reactor projects from ten companies with a target of criticality by July 4, 2026. The U.S. Geological Survey recently added uranium to its Critical Minerals list, reinforcing government concern about supply chain exposure. Sprott sees uranium spot prices stabilising in the $120–$140/lb range as long-term utility contracting accelerates.

headline: CHINA'S SOLAR BUILDOUT DRIVES 790+ TONNE SILVER IMPORT SURGE — STRUCTURAL DEFICIT TOPS 800M OZ
snippet: China imported over 790 tonnes of silver in early 2026, driven primarily by photovoltaic panel manufacturing at scale, according to GoldSeek's weekly Gold SWOT analysis. The four-year cumulative silver market deficit has now surpassed 800 million ounces, with mine supply growing too slowly to offset industrial and investment demand. Despite Thursday's CPI-driven price washout, the structural supply-demand case for silver over the medium term remains one of the strongest in the commodity complex.

headline: SPROTT: URANIUM SPOT RECLAIMS $100/LB AS DENISON'S WHEELER RIVER WINS REGULATORY APPROVAL
snippet: Uranium enters 2026 with renewed momentum as spot prices push back above $100/lb, with Sprott targeting a gradual move to the $120–$140/lb range on tightening supply and accelerating long-term utility contracting. Denison Mines received final regulatory approval to construct the Wheeler River project in Saskatchewan — Canada's first uranium mine to use in-situ recovery — with production expected by mid-2028. The Sprott outlook flags U.S. policy support and critical minerals designation as structural tailwinds that were absent in the 2022–23 bull run.
